issues.issue: Is the claimant a stateless Palestinian?
issues.applicant_position: Claimant says he is a stateless Palestinian, born in the UAE to a Palestinian father and holding Lebanese travel documents.
issues.result_quote: the claimant has established that he is a stateless person, because that evidence shows that he was born in the UAE from a Palestinian father.

issues.issue: Which countries are his countries of former habitual residence for the purposes of the claim?
issues.applicant_position: Counsel argues only Lebanon should count, as it is the only country he can return to and where he got his travel documents.
issues.result_quote: his two countries of former habitual residence are the United Arab Emirates (UAE) and Jordan

issues.issue: Does the claimant face a well-founded fear of persecution in Jordan as a Palestinian without proper documents?
issues.applicant_position: Claimant says as a Palestinian without documents he cannot work or live decently in Jordan, and fears persecution there.
issues.result_quote: The claimant has established a well-founded fear of persecution in Jordan, as a Palestinian.

issues.issue: Does the claimant face a risk of cruel and unusual treatment in the UAE on return?
issues.applicant_position: Claimant says he cannot re-enter the UAE without documents and would face harsh detention there.
issues.result_quote: the tribunal concludes that he has established, on the balance of probabilities, in the UAE, a risk of cruel and unusual punishment due to the detention conditions
